executive.narrative: In January 2026, UX decisions contributed an estimated $61,000 in cost value, helped ship 14 features on time, and established research coverage across 62% of design decisions — laying the foundation for a strong Q1 across Feed, Reels, and DMs.

topDecisions.title: DMs Feature Survey (88% response rate) gave clear direction for improvement priorities
topDecisions.body: 21 of 24 creator panel participants responded to the DMs Feature Survey — identifying the most confusing chat flows and focusing Q1 improvement efforts where they matter most.
topDecisions.outcome: Clear prioritization signal from 88% of panel participation

topDecisions.title: Feed Creator Panel surfaced UX gaps before Q1 dev sprint kicked off
topDecisions.body: Panel session with 78 creators across 55 cohorts identified friction points in the new Feed ranking controls ahead of Q1 development. Adjustments were incorporated into design specs before engineering began.
topDecisions.outcome: Issues resolved in design, not in production

executive.narrative: In February 2026, UX decisions contributed an estimated $101,200 in cost value. The Feed Creator Panel demo drove a 12% increase in feature activations in 10 days — confirming that showing creators their feedback incorporated creates measurable product impact.

topDecisions.title: Feed Creator Panel demo drove 12% increase in activations in 10 days
topDecisions.body: Director of Product and Director of Engineering confirmed new Feed controls adoption is up 12% in 10 days. The increase was attributed to the panel demo — creators seeing their feedback incorporated visibly changed engagement behavior.
topDecisions.outcome: 12% increase in Feed feature activations in 10 days

topDecisions.title: Reels navigation IA V2 validated — 85.6% task success, up from 67.1%
topDecisions.body: The second round of Reels tree testing (n=10, screened creators) achieved 85.6% overall task success — an 18.5% improvement over V1. Four participants achieved 100%. Labeling friction dropped significantly, confirming the tab structure was directionally correct.
topDecisions.outcome: +18.5% task success improvement over V1 baseline

executive.narrative: In March 2026, UX decisions contributed an estimated $212,500 in cost value — including a $150,000 POC kill that prevented a misdirected full build. Design sprint lead reached 71%, keeping engineering unblocked across Feed, Reels, and DMs.

topDecisions.title: POC killed after validation testing — $150,000 in build cost avoided
topDecisions.body: A Stories remix concept in active prototyping failed validation testing against creator expectations. UX research surfaced fundamental misalignment between the proposed flow and how creators think about attribution. The POC was killed before engineering began, avoiding an estimated $150K build.

topDecisions.title: Sprint lead at 71% — design ahead of engineering across most projects
topDecisions.body: Design ran ahead of engineering in 71% of active projects in March, ensuring dev teams had validated specs before sprint kickoff. This reduced mid-sprint design changes and prevented downstream rework across Feed, DMs, and Reels.
topDecisions.outcome: Engineering unblocked — rework risk down quarter-over-quarter

executive.narrative: In April 2026, UX decisions prevented an estimated $76,400 in avoidable spend, helped ship 18 validated features on time, and blocked two product directions that would have required significant rework in engineering.

topDecisions.title: DMs abandoned a complex filter architecture after UXR showed users couldn't discover it
topDecisions.body: A planned multi-level inbox filter was killed in week 2 of April after usability testing with 6 participants showed 0% task completion. Engineering had budgeted 3 sprints. UX redirected to a progressive disclosure pattern that tested at 78% success in the same session.

topDecisions.title: Feed design review caught a carousel truncation bug before dev handoff
topDecisions.body: During a design review of the Feed carousel module, a UX designer identified that the proposed card layout would crop captions on standard phone widths. The fix took 2 hours in Figma. The equivalent engineering fix in production was estimated at 3 days.

topDecisions.title: Reels onboarding flow redesigned based on journey mapping findings
topDecisions.body: A journey mapping session with 4 Reels creators surfaced a consistent point of failure in first-time publishing flows. The original flow required 7 steps for a task creators expected to complete in 2. The redesigned flow reduced steps by 57% and reached stakeholder sign-off in the same sprint.
topDecisions.outcome: Flow complexity reduced 57%; stakeholder sign-off in-sprint

strategicContributions.title: Reels bulk trim actions
strategicContributions.problem: Creators had to trim clips one at a time, making long edits slow and error-prone.
strategicContributions.evidence: 78% of tested creators expected multi-select trim; edit sessions averaged 4.2 min for batch work.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Introduce multi-select with a bulk trim bar and clear selection state before building advanced timeline features.
strategicContributions.outcome: Blocked downstream timeline work until the interaction model is agreed; prototype validated with the Reels panel.

strategicContributions.title: Explore topic filtering
strategicContributions.problem: Users could not filter Explore results by topic cluster, forcing manual scanning of long grids.
strategicContributions.evidence: Ranking limitation surfaced during research; 6 of 8 participants abandoned the task.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Resolve the taxonomy constraint before shipping the redesigned Explore filter panel.
strategicContributions.outcome: Flagged as a blocker to the Explore redesign; engineering scoping in progress.

strategicContributions.title: Spark AI confidence labels
strategicContributions.problem: Creators could not judge how much to trust AI caption suggestions, reducing adoption of Spark AI.
strategicContributions.evidence: Panel sessions showed hesitation and repeated manual rewriting of AI output.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Add confidence labels, edit previews, and fallback states to an already-shipping surface.
strategicContributions.outcome: Enhanced a live experience; trust and repeat usage improved in follow-up testing.

strategicContributions.title: Sign-up flow rework
strategicContributions.problem: Account creation had a high drop-off rate, limiting new user activation.
strategicContributions.evidence: Funnel analysis showed a 34% drop at the username step.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Rework the step sequencing and guidance on the current sign-up flow.
strategicContributions.outcome: Enhanced a high-traffic flow; drop-off reduced in the redesigned path.

strategicContributions.title: Quantifying UX dashboard
strategicContributions.problem: Leadership had no consistent way to see UX's contribution, so its impact stayed invisible in planning conversations.
strategicContributions.evidence: Monthly reviews relied on anecdotes; there was no shared view of research coverage, delivery, and influence.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Build a single dashboard that quantifies UX contribution across research, delivery, and business impact.
strategicContributions.outcome: Enhanced how leadership sees UX; contribution is now legible and tracked month over month.

strategicContributions.title: Making Prism AI-ready
strategicContributions.problem: AI-assisted design drifts from Prism because tokens carry values without usage intent — agents make logical-but-wrong choices.
strategicContributions.evidence: Components meant to be identical diverge across screens; agents read values but not when or why to apply them.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Structure Prism in three layers: tokens, intent metadata, and guardrail docs that constrain agent decisions.
strategicContributions.outcome: Early opportunity to make the system agent-ready, cutting AI-generated design debt across sessions.

strategicContributions.title: Stories creation zero-state
strategicContributions.problem: New creators faced an empty Stories camera with no guidance on where to start.
strategicContributions.evidence: Early concept testing surfaced confusion and low first-session publish success.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Explore zero-state patterns and example templates as a new capability.
strategicContributions.outcome: New opportunity to improve first-run experience; concept validated for further investment.

strategicContributions.title: Safety notification patterns
strategicContributions.problem: Users felt anxious interpreting account restriction messages presented in technical language.
strategicContributions.evidence: Qualitative sessions surfaced repeated confusion and elevated task stress.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Prototype plain-language safety patterns as a new, unmet-need direction.
strategicContributions.outcome: Opportunity to reduce user anxiety; early patterns tested positively.

strategicContributions.title: Creator Studio panel groupings
strategicContributions.problem: Dense Creator Studio screens forced heavy scrolling, slowing creators during high-volume publishing.
strategicContributions.evidence: Session recordings showed repeated long scrolls to reach common panels; task time suffered.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Regroup studio panels by frequency and task, collapsing rarely used sections.
strategicContributions.outcome: Optimization that cut scrolling and sped up common publishing tasks.

strategicContributions.title: Cross-product design tokens
strategicContributions.problem: Inconsistent spacing and color across Instagram surfaces slowed delivery and review.
strategicContributions.evidence: Audit found 40+ divergent values for the same intent across teams.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Standardize a shared Prism token set to simplify and speed up existing work.
strategicContributions.outcome: Reduced rework and sped up handoff across Feed, Reels, and DMs teams.

strategicContributions.title: Activity center consolidation
strategicContributions.problem: Notifications were spread across surfaces, adding noise and maintenance overhead.
strategicContributions.evidence: Support tickets cited duplicate and conflicting alerts for likes, mentions, and follows.
strategicContributions.recommendation: Consolidate into one activity center to simplify the existing experience.
strategicContributions.outcome: Simplified the surface and reduced duplicate alerts.
